newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macquarie plans HQ move in Sydney.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macquarie plans HQ move in Sydney.

text.p: Investment bank Macquarie Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to move out of its current headquarters in the Australian Stock Exchange building and into the GPO development in Sydney's Martin Place in late 1999, with a 15 year lease agreement.

Macquarie said it had finalised negotiations with Melbourne developer Grocon Pty Ltd and its subsidiary Number One Martin Place Ltd to take a 15-year lease over 16 floors in a new office tower and hotel re-development at 1 Martin Place.
The redevelopment included the restoration of the 1897 heritage-listed GPO (General Post Office) building, a 472-room five star hotel and a 27-level office tower and retail complex.
The new buildings would face into a glass atrium, which would feature restaurants, a food hall and an underground ballroom.

"The Bank will lease approximately 25,000 square metres of the office tower with the balance of the building -- approximately 12,600 square metres -- being let by the developer to other tenants," Macquarie said.
Macquarie currently leases about 25,000 square metres at its Bond street premises.
The new building would be completed by mid-1999, allowing Macquarie to move into the new building through the last half of that year.
Macquarie's current lease at the stock exchange building on Bond Street expires in 1999.
It said Martin Place would house about 80 percent of its staff.

Macquarie currently employs about 2,000 staff, in offices located in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Cairns, Auckland, Beijing, Hong Kong, Jakarta, London, Munich, New York, Shanghai, Singapore, Tianjin, and Wellington.
